items.title: You are being rebuilt right now

fact.text: Your body makes about 2.4 million new red blood cells every second.
The Big Bang made only the lightest elements. The carbon, oxygen and iron in you were forged later, inside stars.

items.title: If the universe were one year old

fact.text: Squeeze the universe's whole history into one calendar year, and the time since the last ice age fits into the final 23 seconds of December 31st.
The sunlight on your skin left the Sun about 8 minutes ago.
Earth has about three trillion trees: more than the 100 to 400 billion stars in the whole Milky Way.
A honey bee that finds flowers dances back at the hive, and the angle and length of her waggle tell the others which way to fly and how far.
Snowflakes tend toward six-fold symmetry because ice itself is built as a hexagonal crystal.
Lasers bounced off mirrors left on the Moon show it moving about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.

items.title: Hearing space ripple

fact.text: On 14 September 2015, detectors on Earth first caught ripples in spacetime itself, from two black holes merging about 1.4 billion light-years away.
fact.cite: Wikipedia: First observation of gravitational waves

fact.text: Your brain is about 2% of your body weight, yet it uses up to 20% of your body's energy.
A Great Basin bristlecone pine in California called Methuselah is more than 4,800 years old.
Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal: up to 150,000 hairs in every square centimetre.
From the ground a rainbow looks like an arc, but from a plane, with enough mist below, you can see it as a full circle.
A single teaspoon of productive soil can hold anywhere from 100 million to 3 billion bacteria.
Arctic terns fly from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year, seeing two summers. Birds from Iceland and Greenland average about 70,900 km a round trip.

items.title: A coat that grows a garden

fact.text: A sloth's grooved hair hosts green algae, which tint its coat to blend into the trees.
Axolotls can regrow whole limbs, gills, and even parts of their eyes and brain.

items.title: A map in the magnetic field

fact.text: Sea turtles find their way across open ocean using Earth's magnetic field. Some females come back to nest on the very beach where they hatched.
Elephants recognise themselves in a mirror, a sign of self-awareness shown by only a few animals, including some apes and dolphins.

items.title: Toolmakers

fact.text: New Caledonian crows make their own tools, and can even shape twigs into hooks.

fact.text: Our eyes have four types of light-sensing cell. A mantis shrimp's have between 12 and 16.
Bar-tailed godwits fly from Alaska to New Zealand across the Pacific without stopping: the longest known non-stop flight of any bird.
Dolphins can sleep with one half of the brain at a time, keeping the other half alert, and the eye on the sleeping side closed.
Each June in the Great Smoky Mountains, one firefly species flashes in unison, sending waves of light and dark through the forest.

items.title: A forest that is one tree

fact.text: Pando, in Utah, looks like a grove of about 47,000 aspens. They're all one tree, connected by a single root system.
Touch a sensitive plant and its leaves fold inward and droop, then open again a few minutes later.
Some bamboo can grow 91 cm in a single day: about a millimetre every 90 seconds.
Welwitschia grows just two leaves in its whole life, and some plants are thousands of years old. In Afrikaans its name means 'two leaves, can't die'.
General Sherman, a giant sequoia in California, is the largest known living single-stem tree on Earth by volume.
A dandelion seed's fluffy parachute creates a special ring of swirling air that stays attached above it, carrying it far on the wind.
In 2005, scientists sprouted a 2,000-year-old date palm seed: the oldest seed ever germinated with human help.
Rafflesia arnoldii produces the largest individual flower on Earth.
About 70% of plant species partner with fungi whose threads grow right into their roots, trading sugar for water and nutrients.
Water beads up on a lotus leaf and rolls off, picking up dirt as it goes, thanks to a microscopic surface texture.
Hyperion, a coast redwood in California, is the tallest known living tree: 116.22 metres when measured in 2026.
A female whale shark can keep sperm from a single mating and give birth to pups gradually, over a long period. One was found carrying about 300 pups.
The gastric-brooding frog swallowed her eggs and raised them in her stomach, which stopped making acid while the young grew. The froglets left through her mouth.

items.title: Colours for every stage of life

fact.text: Ribbon eels change colour as they grow: jet black when young, bright blue as adult males, and yellow as the larger females.
Hoatzin chicks have two claws on each wing.

items.title: A lizard disguised as a leaf

fact.text: The satanic leaf-tailed gecko of Madagascar has a flattened tail shaped like a leaf.
The mimic octopus is one of the only animals known to impersonate several others: it can pass for a lionfish, a sea snake or a jellyfish by reshaping its arms and body.
Leafy seadragons are covered in long, leaf-like flaps, and, as with seahorses, it is the father who carries the eggs.

items.title: Sharpshooters

fact.text: Archerfish spit jets of water to knock insects off leaves, hitting targets up to 3 metres above the surface.

fact.text: You can see a glass frog's heart and organs through its belly. When it sleeps, it hides most of its blood in its liver, so it turns even more see-through.
In seahorses, the female places up to 1,500 eggs in the male's brood pouch, and he carries them.
A giraffe's long neck has the same number of neck vertebrae as yours: seven, like most mammals. Each one is just much longer.
Superb lyrebirds mimic the calls of other birds, and even car alarms, chainsaws and camera shutters.
